proEntry.name: Alfredo Duno
proEntry.summary: Signed by the Cincinnati Reds on January 15, 2023.
proEntry.bonusEvidence: One of the top overall prospects in the 2023 international class and the second-highest ranked catcher, Duno got $3.1 million from the Reds when the signing period opened that January. He raised the excitement bar, especially offensively, by raking in the Dominican Summer League. The Reds thought he was advanced enough to push him to full-season ball in 2024, but he never really got to show what he could do, playing just 32 games because of a broken rib. He returned to Daytona in 2025 and helped cement his place among catching prospects by leading the Florida State League in homers, on-base percentage, slugging and OPS. He also hit four homers in a three-game span in the Arizona Fall League to cap things off.

proEntry.name: Aron Estrada
proEntry.summary: Signed by the Baltimore Orioles on January 15, 2022.
proEntry.bonusEvidence: Estrada was a sleeper $175,000 signing out of Venezuela as part of the Orioles’ 2022 international haul, but he’s grown into one of the most exciting prospects from that class by performing at every level he’s been challenged at so far. Estrada put himself on the map with a big debut in the Dominican Summer League, climbed to High-A as a teenager and took another step forward in 2025, reaching Double-A as a 20-year-old and hitting .300/.355/.500 in his first 27 games at the level. Opposing clubs have frequently targeted Estrada in trade talks in recent years, and that shouldn’t change after he produced an .813 OPS and 34 steals across two levels last season.

proEntry.name: Asbel Gonzalez
proEntry.summary: Signed by the Kansas City Royals on January 15, 2023.
proEntry.bonusEvidence: Gonzalez was part of the Royals’ 2023 international signing class and joined the organization for $157,500. The 6-foot-2 outfielder made his stateside debut in 2024 and his full-season debut in ‘25, when he logged 115 games and 415 at-bats for Single-A Columbia. Gonzalez slashed .239/.365/.289 with 12 doubles, three triples and one homer, along with a whopping 78 stolen bases. However, he was also caught stealing 26 times.
